per_pair.why: B's framed title with gold border, clear call-to-action, and cohesive dungeon environment strongly outweigh A's appealing but isolated character artwork mixed with jarring pixelated text.
B demonstrates clean menu-state transitions with consistent visual treatment, while A offers no visible differentiation between navigation states and relies on the same static artwork.
B's well-structured settings menu with clear labeling, functional sliders, and control instructions feels finished and professional, while A just overlays text on the same static background.

loser_biggest_gap: Game A must unify its visual language—the smooth, painted character illustration clashes severely with the jagged, pixelated title text. Choose one consistent direction (either smooth illustration throughout or pure pixel art) and commit to it.
loser_other_gaps: Add a clear, prominent call-to-action (like 'PRESS START') that's immediately visible on the title screen.
Develop distinct visual treatments for different menu states instead of reusing the same static artwork for navigation and settings.
Establish a sense of place or world—the character portrait in isolation feels disconnected from any game context, whereas the dungeon environment draws players in.
reasoning: Game B presents a polished, cohesive title experience with excellent visual hierarchy: a framed title, clear call-to-action, engaging environment backdrop, and professional UI treatment that carries through to settings. Every screen feels intentional and finished. Game A has artistic merit in its character illustration but undermines itself with stylistic inconsistency (smooth art + pixelated text), lack of visual feedback for menu states, and no clear inviting moment. B's pixel-art world draws you in and makes pressing Start feel inevitable; A's isolated character feels incomplete and disconnected.
